headline: Committee hears tiny-home village update and storm damage to parks

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee
meeting.voteItem: Update on Maui's first kauhale (tiny-home village) community
meeting.summary: The committee heard updates on a 64-home tiny-home village for homeless people and on storm damage to county parks, including the closed Kula gym.
meeting.recap: The committee heard an update on a 64-home tiny-home village for people who are homeless.[[0:13:29]] Each tiny home is 100 square feet and has air conditioning.[[0:16:48]] The village received 538 applications in its first eight months.[[0:26:20]] Residents pay a program fee of $450 a month, all included.[[1:08:10]] Three residents have moved into permanent housing so far.[[1:27:19]] The committee deferred the housing item, meaning it was held for later, with no objections.[[1:28:06]] Only one contractor bid to tarp the open part of the gym, at $1.9 million.[[1:31:18]] The department said FEMA left parks out of its categories of work for this storm event.[[1:38:44]] A Kula resident asked whether the gym will be rebuilt, and when.[[1:45:51]] Parks said it has no timeline yet for the gym.[[1:56:08]] Repair costs may be repaid six to nine months after full invoices go to FEMA.[[1:58:24]]
decided: The committee deferred the update on the tiny-home village with no objections.
The chair asked for objections to deferring the parks storm update; the captions do not record a reply.
meeting.next: The chair said a member's question about two other converted facilities will be sent in writing. A member asked the Parks Department to keep the council informed about the Kula gym, and the department agreed.

moments.q: Three exits into permanent housing, none to the streets
$1.9 million bid to tarp the gym

issues.oneLine: A nonprofit runs a 64-home tiny-home village for people who are homeless.
issues.why: The nonprofit's leader called it the community's first development for deeply affordable housing.
issues.next: The nonprofit's chief executive officer said he can get the breakdown of who paid for the village.
issues.brief: About 80% of applicants are single men and 20% are women.[[#1]] The village opened to residents in December and became full last month.[[#2]] Residents sign a six-month program agreement that can be renewed monthly.[[#3]] Applicants are taken on a first-come, first-served basis.[[#4]]

issues.oneLine: Storms damaged county parks, and the Kula gym remains closed.
issues.why: The department said FEMA leaving parks out of its categories of work affects financial recovery.

deadlines.t: Emergency work projects submitted to FEMA with all costs.

issues.brief: Parks said there is no other gym close by for Kula kids to use.[[#1]] Repairing a golf course driving range is estimated to cost $657,000.[[#2]] Parks said tree removal so far has been paid from its general fund budget.[[#3]]
